text:
alex_g: Quick heads-up — I rolled the kernel-selection tweak earlier for canary traffic and I'm seeing a small p95 regression on short sequences. p50 unchanged. Anyone else seeing a tail bump?

maria_k: saw the spike in the dashboard at ~16:29 UTC. p95 up ~8ms. KV hit rate basically stable (0.67 -> 0.66). Could be batch formation changing.

daniel_r: can you paste the replay command + config you used?

alex_g: replay command used:
```
tools/replay --trace=canary-2026-03-16 --kernel=opt-v2 --batch-window-ms=5 --jitter-ms=2 --token-budget=128
```
Policy we pushed: `staggered_window: true, base_interval_ms:5, jitter_ms:2, max_wait_ms:12`

kevin_ops: FYI infra auto-switched some hosts to `opt-v2-fp16` when it detected older cudnn on that pool — kernel switching could add overhead during hot path.

sophie_w: I sampled a few tail requests; stack trace shows extra memcpy in kernel_bind() path. Looks like kernel selection/probing occurring inline for some requests.

ci-bot: deploy: canary config applied to 10 hosts (canary-3123). Health: 10/10.

maria_k: numbers from replay vs prod snapshot:
- replay p50: 18ms -> 18ms
- replay p95: 95ms -> 103ms (+8ms)
- kv_hit_rate: 0.67 -> 0.66
- avg_tokens_per_batch: 72 -> 70

alex_g: my working hypothesis — the jitter profile is causing more interleaving of short requests so virtual batches span mixed kernels, leading to extra kernel bind/memcpy overhead and raising tail latency.

daniel_r: simple test: disable jitter (jitter_ms=0) and increase base_interval to 6ms so batches form a bit more deterministically; also pin kernel to avoid on-request probing.

kevin_ops: I'm spinning a canary with `staggered_window: false, base_interval_ms:6, jitter_ms:0` and pinning kernel to `opt-v2-no-probe` on those hosts.

sophie_w: long-term we should move kernel probing out-of-path to an async background probe. For now pinning is a safe mitigation. Also add a micro-span around kernel_select() in tracing.

alex_g: good call. Also adding a `token_budget_target` trace metric so we can see token budget vs actual batch size per request.

maria_k: created a short A/B job: A=staggered+jitter (baseline), B=no-probe+pinned+slightly-larger-window. Running 1h replay against both.

kevin_ops: canary B started at 16:51 UTC (hosts: canary-3123b). Pin applied, logs show no probe events.

ci-bot: perf-check: canary B preliminary after 20m: p95 -3ms vs baseline, p50 stable. KV hit rate unchanged.

daniel_r: nice — if B stays better, we should default probe to async and expose sync probe as an opt-in flag.

sophie_w: also adding micro-profiling spans around memcpy+kernel_bind in the serving boundary so we can attribute time to infra vs runtime kernels.

alex_g: opened draft PR with toggles and tracing additions: https://git/repo/PR-456 — PTAL.

maria_k: PR looks good, merging if canary holds for 1h.

kevin_ops: plan to roll to 50% after 1h if metrics green :rocket:.

alex_g: thanks all — will follow up tomorrow with full replay numbers and kernel-probe async proposal.
